title: `kit-shrine-sigil_mark`: Sigil mark, shrine
notes:
- **Mode:** Kit sprite, 256 x 256 transparent sprite, NEW.
- **Save as:** `art/sprites/kit/shrine/sigil_mark.png`.
- **Shows:** Survival fight maps, shrine and cathedral district; a Sigil word drawn into the world long ago (a door carving, a Keystone, a warding post, an old plate), investigated from the next tile. A plain star today.
paint: Setting: shrine, shrine and cathedral district (pale flagstone, dark wood, ivory wax, violet cloth, gold #F2C46A candle glow). One Sigil mark sprite, flat on the ground, non-blocking, about two thirds of a tile: a carved pale flagstone with an abstract glyph of nested arcs inlaid in gold leaf, the gold worn thin at the centre, a drip of ivory wax beside it. It is old, worn and only slightly lit, an abstract glyph and never a letter; it shows a deliberate old mark, not damage. At 64 px: a worn plate or stone with one clear carved shape at its centre. It must differ from the poi (this one is a fixed carving, not an object lying on the floor) and from the Sigil wall (no flecks, no glow). Avoid: letters, numerals, a real religion's symbol, a bright glow, a person.
paintExtra: One small isolated worn inset plate or stone only. Capture the shallow flush carving directly overhead, with the glyph as an incised surface detail. Transparent surroundings, no large tile, no halo, no dust vignette. Do not paint a glowing mark.
label: Sigil mark, shrine
prompt:
Paint one game-map kit piece in Heavenprint: hand-painted gouache and ink with broken, directional brush strokes, selective dry-brush scumbling, restrained hatching and warm ivory accents, the same hand as the attached kit pieces, but simplified and bold so it reads at 64 px. Straight overhead view, no perspective tilt, no horizon. Flat, even top light with one consistent soft highlight from the upper left on edges and tops; NO cast shadow, NO drop shadow, NO ground contact shadow, NO glow or bloom spilling outside the object (a lamp, a seam or the flecks the piece names may be lit within the object's own shape, never as a halo). Scale: one tile = 1.5 m = 256 px; a crate is about a metre (about 170 px), a standing person's footprint about a third of a tile. No text, no letters, no numbers, no signs with writing, no logos, no figures, no creatures, no UI, no frame, no border, no watermark. Everything is invented. For a sprite: transparent background (PNG with alpha), the object centred inside an 80% safe box of a 256 x 256 px canvas, crisp clean edges, no halo, nothing touching the canvas edge. For a ground texture: a seamless tileable square texture, 1024 x 1024 px, straight top-down, the left and right edges match and the top and bottom edges match when repeated, flat even lighting, no vignette, no border, no landmark that would show as a repeat, no objects on it, even mid-dark value with gentle low-contrast variation. The piece:
Setting: shrine, shrine and cathedral district (pale flagstone, dark wood, ivory wax, violet cloth, gold #F2C46A candle glow). One Sigil mark sprite, flat on the ground, non-blocking, about two thirds of a tile: a carved pale flagstone with an abstract glyph of nested arcs inlaid in gold leaf, the gold worn thin at the centre, a drip of ivory wax beside it. It is old, worn and only slightly lit, an abstract glyph and never a letter; it shows a deliberate old mark, not damage. At 64 px: a worn plate or stone with one clear carved shape at its centre. It must differ from the poi (this one is a fixed carving, not an object lying on the floor) and from the Sigil wall (no flecks, no glow). Avoid: letters, numerals, a real religion's symbol, a bright glow, a person.
Center glyph is exactly TWO curved concentric gold grooves with ends open to the UPPER RIGHT like a pair of quarter-circle crescents turned together, irregular hand-carved width. No additional mark, no dot, no centered circular shape, and no Wi-Fi symbol. Keep the tiny wax drip visibly separate near the stone edge.
